item.title: Clean-Room Reverse-Engineering Findings from Stock Google Jamboard ROM
item.description: Overview This document records the clean-room interoperability findings obtained from inspecting partition backups (stock-system.img, stock-vendor.img, and stock-wifi-rp3.img) pulled from a Google Jamboard (baracus) running Google’s final End-of-Life Android 7.0 release (google/baracus/baracus:7.0/NRT1.240624.004/12020658:user/release-keys). The primary goal of this investigation was to determine how Google’s stock OS distinguished between fingers, the passive stylus, and the passive microfiber eraser (or any other eraser/palm), and why unmodified AOSP/LineageOS and mainline Linux kernels only expose basic finger touch.
